title: Duskapple Orchard - The Fallen Star (SNES register)
_note: The hometown lullaby, darkened: Tinderwick's Vesper statement (G3->C4->D4 lift, settle home) moved into the PARALLEL minor (C minor) and slowed into a half-time feel at 90 BPM, so every motif note is twice as long and the lift hangs in the cold air. Plays in Duskapple Orchard from the first visit until the first Gleam is relit (tinderwick-c, the hopeful sibling, takes over after). A star fell here: one distant low BELL toll at each phrase start (the strike), a glassy celesta ostinato for the cold, sparse low STRINGS. Bridge (bars 9-12): a faint warm glimmer - Ab and Eb major, a PLUCK harp warmth, the lead lifts to its highest note (the cinder still glows) - then sinks back to the G dominant before the return. snes era (warm reverb). 90 BPM, 4/4, C minor, 16 bars AABA. Melancholy and beautiful, not horror.

tracks.name: lead
tracks._note: Muted low pulse lead. The Vesper contour in C minor at half time: A states the lift and the minor settle (Eb-D-C); A' half-cadences on D over G; B reaches up to G4 (the glimmer) and sinks; A'' returns, last bar C4->B3 leading back to the G3 downbeat.

tracks.name: glass
tracks._note: Cold glassy celesta ostinato, slow quarter-note broken chords high above the lead (oct 5) - the frost on the charred boughs. Rests through the bridge so the warm pluck can glow, returns for A''.
